title: Short-term disability: evidence checklist
text:
This synthetic guidance lists the documents an examiner normally expects in a short-term disability claim file. It is administrative: it helps prepare the file and never decides eligibility or benefit amounts.

Expected items: the claimant statement with the last day worked, the employer statement with job title, scheduled hours and earnings period, and the attending provider statement with restrictions and an expected return-to-work date.

Flag as missing when the attending provider statement has no restrictions section, when the last day worked differs between the claimant and employer statements, or when the earnings period is not stated. Record the conflict; do not resolve it.

title: Long-term disability: evidence checklist
text:
Synthetic examiner guidance for long-term disability files. The assistant summarises what was received and lists gaps for a human examiner.

Expected items: the short-term disability history where one exists, the occupational description from the employer, recent treating provider records covering the elimination period, and any functional capacity evaluation.

Flag gaps such as treating records that stop before the end of the elimination period, an occupational description without physical demands, or a functional capacity evaluation that is referenced but not attached.

title: Life claims: evidence checklist
text:
Synthetic guidance for preparing life claim files. The examiner confirms all findings; the assistant never decides validity or payment.

Expected items: the claimant statement, a certified death certificate, the beneficiary designation on file, and proof of identity for each named beneficiary.

Flag as missing or conflicting when the name or date of birth on the certificate differs from the policy record, when a beneficiary has no identity document, or when the designation on file is older than a later change request mentioned in correspondence.

title: Accident claims: evidence checklist
text:
Synthetic guidance for accident claim files. Causation is never determined by the assistant.

Expected items: the incident report with date, time and location, the first treatment record, and any police or workplace incident reference that the claimant mentions.

Flag when the incident date differs between the report and the first treatment record, when a referenced police report is not attached, or when the first treatment is more than the documented delay after the incident and no explanation is on file.

title: Critical illness: evidence checklist
text:
Synthetic guidance for critical illness files. The assistant does not interpret diagnoses; it lists what was received.

Expected items: the claimant statement, the specialist report naming the condition and the date it was confirmed, and supporting test results referenced in the report.

Flag when the specialist report references tests that are not attached, when the confirmation date is missing, or when the condition named in the claim form differs from the specialist report.

title: Dental claims: evidence checklist
text:
Synthetic guidance for dental claim files.

Expected items: the itemised treatment statement with procedure codes and dates, the provider details, and pre-treatment estimates where the plan uses them.

Flag when a procedure on the statement has no date, when the provider details are incomplete, or when the treated amount differs from an attached pre-treatment estimate. Report amounts only as received; never calculate a benefit.

title: Examiner handoff: structure and boundaries
text:
Synthetic guidance for the handoff the assistant drafts for a human claims examiner.

Structure: case summary from supplied facts only, evidence received, missing or conflicting items specific to the case, and suggested next administrative steps such as requesting a document.

Boundaries: never decide coverage, eligibility, exclusions, diagnosis, causation, fraud, entitlement, claim validity or benefit amount. The field benefit_determination is always 'Not determined'. A human examiner makes every settlement decision.
